fix_commit_message:
avcodec/h2645_sei: Initialize side data before deallocation

Fixes: use after free
Fixes: poc_hvcc_modified.mp4

Found by: Jiale Yao
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f435ce22e10e on top of intro 6d0c89980c78 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): In libavcodec/h2645_sei.c, the function h2645_sei_to_side_data() handles conversion of parsed HEVC/H.264 SEI messages (including Ambient Viewing Environment) into AVFrameSideData. For the Ambient Viewing Environment SEI, code allocates an AVAmbientViewingEnvironment struct, wraps it in an AVBufferRef, and calls ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext() to attach it as frame side data, transferring ownership of the buffer. Only after this call does the code populate the struct's ambient_illuminance/ambient_light_x/ambient_light_y fields. Because ownership of the underlying buffer can already be transferred or the buffer already released as part of that call's internal handling (in success or error paths), writing to dst_env afterwards can operate on memory that could already have been freed/exposed elsewhere, producing a use-after-free. This was found via fuzzing with a crafted MP4/HVCC sample (poc_hvcc_modified.mp4). Root cause: The struct fields for the newly-allocated side-data object are initialized AFTER handing the wrapping buffer off to a function (ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext) that can take ownership of / free that buffer, instead of before. This creates a window in which the memory the code is about to write to is no longer guaranteed to be valid/owned by this code path.
